---
title: "Step 2 QA Actions"
editor: visual
---

This is a non exhaustive list of the types of actions covered in quality assurance. Higher tiers should include checks from lower stages.

### Low (to be carried by peer review)

- Overall ‘sense checks’/spot-checking including conditional formatting and formulas
- Narrative is clear, concise and answers the question asked. Spelling/grammar is professional
- Styling is consistent with team style guide
- Key information is documented – such as source, dates etc.
- Any statements referencing numbers are true and accurate
- Compare recently produced figures to historic QA figures, by cross checking results against other data sources available
- Inclusion of the QA information at the front of the report/product cover page or meta data
- Inclusion of QA Output level with appropriate caveats (Gold/Silver/Bronze)

### Medium (to be carried out by peer, with line manager or equivalent oversight)

- Appropriate checking of data sources / wider contextual factors
- Review of code/syntax where relevant (GitHub recommended). Review of calculations / formula
- Analytical/statistical methods are appropriately selected, applied and interpreted

### High (to be carried out by peer, with line manager oversight and SLT sign-off)

- Complete verification of source data against available information or appropriate QA statement from data provider to give assurance of quality
- Gold checks should be undertaken by two or more analysts not involved in the creation of the original analysis.
- Sufficient time should be allocated to a project, for completion of ‘Gold’ standard checks.

::: {.callout-important appearance="default" icon="true"}
## Important

Note for any analysis being sent to senior colleagues (executives and other senior managers) this should be reviewed by SLT regardless of tier.
:::
